For anyone living outside the US and unfamiliar with this holiday, it was created to memorialize the original European settlers (pilgrims) and their tradition of giving thanks for good fortune, especially following a strong harvest.

I like Thanksgiving because it's become almost entirely about food, and it's one of the least commercialized major American holidays. Nobody's peddling fireworks in gas station parking lots, nobody is pressuring you to dress up as something, most businesses have been gearing up for Christmas since Nov 1, and by default Thanksgiving isn't very conducive to marketing or structure (no mascot like Santa, no attire like Halloween, no mandatory timeframe like New Year's Eve, etc). The only drawback is the higher price for air travel, busier roads, and Black Friday, a thing where Americans wake up early just to go shopping. Let's face it, American corporations will find a way to make everything about them, b/c they're selfish.

Growing up, you see a lot of thanksgiving imagery of pilgrims sharing an Autumn meal with native Americans, about 200-300 years before slaughtering their buffalo and sending them west..then east..then onto reservations...look, every country has a dark past, but today we think back to a time when people were literally just happy to be alive in such a harsh and deadly land. Remember, the people of Roanoke weren't so lucky.
